<a id="s0-p1"></a>[0¶1] This document is the contract for what `pcrec --emit-facts` prints: its sections, their columns, and what is and is not promised about each. It conforms to `docs/spec/table_contract.md` and adds only what is specific to this listing. `docs/spec/cli.md` §2 is the flag's own reference entry. The listing's history is `docs/dev/history/facts_listing_record.md`, which is not normative.

<a id="s1"></a>
## 1. What the listing is

- <a id="s1-p1"></a>[1¶1] It is a DEBUG listing, with `docs/spec/ir_listing.md`'s status: the format and its vocabularies are promised; the row set and the prose are advisory. It is not part of the generated artifact, so it has no `abi` number.
- <a id="s1-p2"></a>[1¶2] It prints the pattern-facts record of a compile: what pcrec concluded about the PATTERN (which construct kinds it contains, whether it can match the empty string, the byte every match must contain, the necessary literal run and set, the start anchor, the bytes a non-empty match can begin with, the end window, the bytes every match carries at each offset from its own start, and where the necessary run sits among them). For each fact it prints the fact's status, whether a pass consumed it, and why it has its value. It also prints the artifact's own decision stamps (which engine, which prefilter, whether a pre-check was emitted), which are route decisions the record does not hold.
- <a id="s1-p3"></a>[1¶3] It reads the record and never recomputes it. A `facts` row is the value, status and reason the fact's accessor stored when the compile asked it. The value is rendered by the same renderer the artifact's fact-valued stamps use (`<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE`, `_REQ_RUN`, `_END_WINDOW`, `_VM_START`), so a stamp and the listing cannot spell one value two ways. The `decisions` rows are read off the finished artifact's text. Only the FINAL compile attempt's record is listed: a record from an attempt the compiler discarded (a retry, a size-ladder rung) is never shown.
- <a id="s1-p4"></a>[1¶4] It is not VM-only: facts are engine-neutral, and the listing works on a DFA, hybrid or VM artifact alike.

<a id="s2"></a>
## 2. The query

- <a id="s2-p1"></a>[2¶1] The form is `pcrec --emit-facts[=ENC,...] [compile options] --pattern P`.
- <a id="s2-p2"></a>[2¶2] It is a QUERY, like `--emit-ir`: it takes a pattern, takes no `-o`, runs the ordinary compile to completion in memory, prints the listing and exits. It composes with no other query mode (`--emit-facts --emit-ir` is refused).
- <a id="s2-p3"></a>[2¶3] Every compile option (`-e`, every `-f`/`-fno-` axis, `--engine`, `--features`, and the rest) applies unchanged, so the listing describes the compile the caller would have got.
- <a id="s2-p4"></a>[2¶4] The bare flag lists one compile under the `-e` in effect. `=ENC,...` (for example `--emit-facts=byte,utf8`) runs one complete, ordinary compile per listed encoding and concatenates their rows under each section, every row carrying its `encoding`.
- <a id="s2-p5"></a>[2¶5] A pattern pcrec refuses is refused with the ordinary compile's diagnostic (exit 1).

<a id="s3"></a>
## 3. Framing

1. <a id="s3-p1"></a>[3¶1] `docs/spec/table_contract.md` applies in full: TAB-separated values, `#` comment lines, the last `#` line before a section's first data row is that section's header, columns are append-only, an empty field means "none", a field never contains a TAB.
2. <a id="s3-p2"></a>[3¶2] Every table is a NAMED `#section`. The preamble before the first `#section` is free prose and belongs to no section.
3. <a id="s3-p3"></a>[3¶3] The section NAME set is the API and is append-only. `facts` and `decisions` exist; no other section is printed.
4. <a id="s3-p4"></a>[3¶4] Cell escaping is `pcrec_sb_text`'s vocabulary, the one every registry dump uses: a byte below 0x20, and 0x7f, goes out as `\xNN`; every other byte passes through as itself.
5. <a id="s3-p5"></a>[3¶5] Column WIDTH is not a contract. Fields are unpadded.
6. <a id="s3-p6"></a>[3¶6] A `#` line never follows a section's data (table contract rule 3 would make it the next section's header).

<a id="s4"></a>
## 4. The sections

<a id="s4-1"></a>
### 4.1 `facts` — `encoding | fact | grain | epoch | status | used | value | why | note`

<a id="s4-1-p1"></a>[4.1¶1] One row per record fact, per listed encoding, in the record's own table order. Every fact the record has is listed, including ones no pass asked for: after the artifact and every stamp are complete, the listing asks each unasked fact once, through the same accessor and derivation, which is why those rows read `used no`. Because the extra asks happen after the artifact exists, they cannot change a byte of it.

| column | content | promised |
|---|---|---|
| `encoding` | the compile's encoding (`-e`'s spelling) | yes |
| `fact` | the fact's name | NO: facts may be added, renamed or split |
| `grain` | `pattern` (one answer per compile; node-grain facts are not listed) | vocabulary yes |
| `epoch` | the seal the fact is asked after: `E1` structural, `E2` lowered, `E3` machine | vocabulary yes |
| `status` | CLOSED: `derived` / `denied` / `declined` / `absent` (§4.1.1) | yes |
| `used` | CLOSED: `yes` — a compiler pass asked for the fact while the artifact was built; `no` — only the listing asked | yes |
| `value` | the fact's value, by its one renderer (§4.1.2) | spellings shared with a stamp are that stamp's (`match_api.md` §6.3, `tuning.md` §2.25-§2.28); others advisory |
| `why` | CLOSED token grammar plus detail (§4.1.3) | the grammar yes; reason NAMES no |
| `note` | prose (the fact's kind and owning source file) | no wording promise (D26) |

<a id="s4-1-1"></a>
#### 4.1.1 `status`

- <a id="s4-1-1-p1"></a>[4.1.1¶1] `derived` — the fact's derivation ran; its value may still be an empty answer (`none`) when the pattern has nothing to find.
- <a id="s4-1-1-p2"></a>[4.1.1¶2] `denied` — a fact-level `-fno-` flag stored the fact's empty value without deriving it (the build is indistinguishable from a pattern with nothing to find, for every consumer of the fact); `why` names the flag.
- <a id="s4-1-1-p3"></a>[4.1.1¶3] `declined` — the derivation ran and declined for a stated structural reason; `why` names it.
- <a id="s4-1-1-p4"></a>[4.1.1¶4] `absent` — the fact is not derivable on this compile's route, or the listing's own forced ask of it failed; its `value` is empty. The `E3` facts are derivable only on a route whose forward scan runs the unanchored machine (`<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN "unanchored"`, a DFA or a hybrid artifact); on every other route they are `absent` with a `decline:` naming the route (§4.1.3), and no pass can have consumed them.

<a id="s4-1-2"></a>
#### 4.1.2 `value`

- <a id="s4-1-2-p1"></a>[4.1.2¶1] A byte is a decimal number. A run is lowercase hex, followed by `@idx` (the scanned member's index) where the stamp carries it, and, only where some position is not an exact byte, by `/` and each position's mask in hex (`tuning.md` §2.28).
- <a id="s4-1-2-p2"></a>[4.1.2¶2] A set is a comma-joined ascending byte list.
- <a id="s4-1-2-p3"></a>[4.1.2¶3] `start_anchor` is `<PREFIX>_VM_START`'s token.
- <a id="s4-1-2-p4"></a>[4.1.2¶4] `kinds` is a comma-joined list of kind names in a fixed order (`bref`, `linked_call`, `var`, `atomic`, `lookaround`, `live_capture`, `collapsible_rep`), or `none`. `lookaround` counts only lookarounds that stay sub-matches: a one-character lookaround is a context node (`tuning.md` §2.32) and is not in it.
- <a id="s4-1-2-p5"></a>[4.1.2¶5] `nullable` and `empty_admits` are `yes` or `no`. `empty_admits` is `yes` when some way of matching the empty string crosses no non-multiline `^`/`\A` or no non-multiline `$`/`\Z`/`\z`; it is `no` on a non-nullable pattern, and on one whose every empty match is confined to a subject empty up to a final newline. The prefilter declines read it (`tuning.md` §2.17).
- <a id="s4-1-2-p6"></a>[4.1.2¶6] `kset_walk` is a comma-joined list of its offsets in order: a one-byte offset as that byte in decimal, a wider one as `[N]`, its byte count.
- <a id="s4-1-2-p7"></a>[4.1.2¶7] `run_pin` is the offset in decimal (a pin on the whole window), or `o:at+len` (a pin on the exact stretch `at .. at+len` of a masked window, `tuning.md` §2.30).
- <a id="s4-1-2-p8"></a>[4.1.2¶8] `req_run_maxoff` is the run window's maximum byte offset from the attempt start, as a decimal or `unbounded` (with `why` `decline:unbounded`). `<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF` carries it where the handoff applies (`tuning.md` §2.41).
- <a id="s4-1-2-p9"></a>[4.1.2¶9] `end_window` is a decimal or `none`.
- <a id="s4-1-2-p10"></a>[4.1.2¶10] `start_set` is a superset of the bytes the first consumed byte of a non-empty match can be, every zero-width node erased, on the encoding-lowered tree. It is `nullable` where the zero-width-erased language can match the empty string (no byte is then necessary), and otherwise its member count, `:`, and the 256-bit set as 64 lowercase hex digits, byte 0 first, bit `b & 7` of byte `b >> 3` for byte value `b` (so `ab` lists `1:` followed by a set whose only bit is 0x61's).
- <a id="s4-1-2-p11"></a>[4.1.2¶11] A fact with no answer renders `none`. The value is EMPTY on an `absent` row.

<a id="s4-1-3"></a>
#### 4.1.3 `why`

<a id="s4-1-3-p1"></a>[4.1.3¶1] `why` is empty for a plain derivation, else exactly one of:

- <a id="s4-1-3-p2"></a>[4.1.3¶2] `deny:<flag>` — `<flag>` is the `-fno-` spelling exactly as `--list-axes` and the CLI accept it (`deny:-fno-req-byte`). Where two flags can deny a fact and both were given, the lower-numbered bit is named.
- <a id="s4-1-3-p3"></a>[4.1.3¶3] `decline:<reason>` — for example `decline:enc-multibyte` (the end window under an encoding with non-boundary positions), `decline:not-end-anchored`, `decline:gstart`, `decline:unbounded`, `decline:force-failed` (the listing's own ask failed; the compile's result is unaffected), `decline:attempt-unwrapped-nfa` (an `E3` fact on a route whose forward scan is the anchored-attempt machine, `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN "attempt"`) and `decline:no-forward-nfa` (an `E3` fact on an artifact with no DFA scan at all).
- <a id="s4-1-3-p4"></a>[4.1.3¶4] `rate:<source>` — for a fact CHOSEN by a byte-rate rule, which rule answered: `rate:builtin-prior` (the shipped byte-frequency prior) or `rate:none(<encoding>)->rightmost` (the prior does not apply to this encoding, and its no-rate answer decided: the candidate with the fewest members, ties to the rightmost, so the rightmost member wherever every candidate is one byte; `findings.md` §4).

<a id="s4-1-3-p5"></a>[4.1.3¶5] Which `-fno-` flag empties which fact is stated, flag by flag, in `docs/spec/tuning.md`'s "Facts emptied" line for that flag, and the listing is checked against that text (`tests/codegen/run_facts_checks.sh`).

<a id="s4-2"></a>
### 4.2 `decisions` — `encoding | stamp | value`

- <a id="s4-2-p1"></a>[4.2¶1] One row per VALUE stamp in the finished artifact, in the order the artifact carries them: every object-like `#define` whose name is `<PREFIX>_…` or `PCREC_FEATURE_…`, read off the artifact's emitted C (compiled without a paired header, so every stamp is in the one `.c` text).
- <a id="s4-2-p2"></a>[4.2¶2] `stamp` is the macro name exactly as emitted; `value` is its replacement text exactly as emitted (a quoted string stays quoted).
- <a id="s4-2-p3"></a>[4.2¶3] The function-like machinery macros a VM artifact defines (`<PREFIX>_PUSH(...)` and its family) are code, not stamps, and are not listed.
- <a id="s4-2-p4"></a>[4.2¶4] What each stamp means is its own spec's (`match_api.md` §6.3, `tuning.md`); this section promises only that it is the artifact's stamp block, byte for byte.

<a id="s5"></a>
## 5. Guarantees

1. <a id="s5-p1"></a>[5¶1] The listing never refuses a compile that succeeded. A forced ask that fails is recorded as that one fact's `absent` / `decline:force-failed` row; the rest of the listing, and the exit status, are the compile's.
2. <a id="s5-p2"></a>[5¶2] The listing never changes the compile. Its only extra work happens after the artifact and every stamp exist, and it reads the record rather than re-deriving anything, so the artifact a `--emit-facts` compile builds is the artifact the same options build without it.
3. <a id="s5-p3"></a>[5¶3] One spelling per value. A fact-valued stamp and the fact's `value` cell come from one renderer.

<a id="s6"></a>
## 6. What is not promised

- <a id="s6-p1"></a>[6¶1] The fact NAMES and the row set (facts may be added, renamed or split).
- <a id="s6-p2"></a>[6¶2] Value spellings beyond those shared with a stamp.
- <a id="s6-p3"></a>[6¶3] `why` reason names beyond the token grammar.
- <a id="s6-p4"></a>[6¶4] `note` text.

<a id="s6-p5"></a>[6¶5] Tools that key on this listing should resolve columns by name and treat unknown facts, sections and trailing columns as ignorable (table contract consumer rules).
